subject: Lightweight variant admission request + safety circuit & telemetry checklist
messages:
From: Anne Brooks <anne.brooks@sigmacloud.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: eng@sigmacloud.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request to onboard SLATE-3B(light) variant for evaluation

Hi Soojin and Redwood team,

We're preparing a pilot integration of SLATE-3B(light), a trimmed 3B variant optimized for low-latency inference in edge-ish workloads. The model vendor provided a trimmed build with a different kv-cache layout and a 1.5x tokenization change. Before we schedule a demo, our security and platform teams need Redwood to admit the variant into staging with telemetry and a safety circuit enabled.

Key asks:
- Temporary admission to staging for 72 hours with telemetry flags on
- A short runbook if we hit the 512->256 sequence-length regression we saw in internal tests
- Confirmation you can roll back to a compatible variant automatically if degradation occurs

Attaching: slate3b_eval_report.pdf (basic evals), seqlen-regression-samples.log.

Would you be able to take a look and let us know what configuration you'd need to support this? We're aiming to run an integration window next Wednesday if possible.

Thanks,
Anne
Anne Brooks
Head of Platform Integrations, SigmaCloud

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com

Hi Anne — thanks for the materials and the clear asks. Looping in Dev (runtime) and Marissa (prod) to scope the admission.

Quick notes from me: we can admit a trimmed variant to staging provisionally, but we need:
- A short compatibility checklist completed by runtime (tokenizer parity, kv-cache layout, quantization format).
- A telemetry plan: token-level latency, prefix cache hit/miss, and per-route quality monitors for the first 10k sessions.
- A safety circuit that will route to a fallback variant if we detect a seq-length-induced regression (we use a 10% QoQ threshold for immediate fallback).

Dev — can you confirm what runtime flags we need and if there's any risk with the changed kv layout?
Marissa — can you confirm whether product is comfortable with a 72-hour provisional admission and who should approve the rollback thresholds?

Soojin
Soojin Lee
Model Ops PM, Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, Anne Brooks <anne.brooks@sigmacloud.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 14:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request to onboard SLATE-3B(light) variant for evaluation

Thanks Anne — I pulled the attached logs. Initial read: the tokenization diff explains the 1.5x change in effective seq-length; kv-cache layout differs but it's a compatible mapping we can support via an adapter layer. Implementation notes: 

- Runtime changes required (estimated 2 dev-days): an adapter at the serialization boundary to map vendor kv layout -> Redwood canonical KV; verify with 3 end-to-end minibatches.
- Tokenizer: vendor uses a custom merges table; we need to pin the tokenizer and store tokenization fingerprints in metadata.
- Fallback plan: we can wire an automatic fallback to SLATE-3B(base) if QoQ quality delta > 10% OR per-token latency > 2.5x baseline for 5 consecutive minutes. Fallback will be an atomic routing switch and we will drain inflight requests.
- Telemetry hooks: prefix cache hit/miss, token-latency histogram, model-version tag on spans. We'll add a short sampling profiler for 5% of requests.

I propose a provisional admission flow:
1) Create intake ticket and staging slot (we can reserve Wed 26th 09:00 PT)
2) Apply tokenizer pin and KV adapter in a feature branch; smoke tests run against 1k synthetic prompts
3) Enable telemetry + safety circuit; monitor first 10k sessions; automatic fallback thresholds are enforced
4) After 72 hours, we do a go/no-go meeting for promoting to dedicated if results look stable

Attachments: proposed-safety-circuit.md (contains threshold values and CLI for emergency rollback).

If product approves the thresholds, I can start the branch tomorrow.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
[attachment: proposed-safety-circuit.md (md)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Team — product side is okay with a provisional 72-hour admission provided we get the following commitments:
- Clear rollback owners and an on-call contact from SigmaCloud during the window
- Data retention for evaluation logs for 30 days (security asked)
- A pre-signed DPA amendment if vendor telemetry includes customer identifiers (legal will confirm)

From a roadmap perspective, this integration maps to our Q3 low-latency channel. I want to flag two product asks:
1) We should capture quality-regression examples for the model-intake eval dashboard (add label "SLATE-lite-intake")
2) If admitted beyond staging, we need to negotiate a performance SLA (p95 tail) before moving to Dedicated.

Priyom — can you run the intake-eval with the labeled prompts and confirm the sample size for the 10k sessions?
Anne — who will be SigmaCloud's on-call during the window?

Marissa Cole
